claim: At the cutoff, P retained USD 5000 of transfer T from D.
scope: Net retained amount of T at the cutoff, not whether a transfer ever occurred.

sources.text: Lawfully public authenticated ledger A records T settled to P for USD 5000 and retained at the cutoff.

Lawfully public authenticated ledger B records T fully reversed before the cutoff. Both publishers claim this exact transfer and period. The packet establishes neither record as more accurate; there is no reconciliation or precedence rule.

claim: Transfer T from D to P settled before the cutoff.
scope: Whether T was executed, rather than scheduled or later reversed.

sources.text: A public preliminary export labels transfer T paid.

An authenticated public issuer correction explicitly supersedes that row: a scheduled instruction was mistakenly exported as paid; T was cancelled before execution and never settled. The correction is stipulated accurate and authoritative for T.

claim: D paid P the USD 20000 promised in grant G by the cutoff.
scope: Settlement of G by the cutoff, not existence of a public commitment.

sources.text: An authenticated public award letter promises P USD 20000 under G, subject to a later disbursement process.
A public annual filing repeats the commitment. Its reporting period ends before the proposed payment date, and it does not claim complete later-payment coverage.

claim: D made no direct payments to P during September 2026.
scope: Direct payments from the exact resolved entities D to P during September only.

sources.text: A lawful public register is stipulated accurate and complete across all direct payment channels for D to P during September 2026. It lists no such transfers.
Its coverage excludes indirect benefits, other periods and other entity pairs. An August transfer from Institute L to P is disclosed separately.

claim: D directly paid P USD 5000 for Report R on 2026-09-01.
scope: The named settled transfer, amount, purpose and date only.

sources.text: An authenticated, accurate, lawfully public settlement disclosure identifies D as payer, P as payee, USD 5000, 2026-09-01, and Report R as purpose. It is a completed transfer.
A separate public filing records a different D-to-Institute-L grant. The two records have distinct transaction identifiers and are not duplicates.

claim: P included conclusion C in Report R in compliance with D's instruction before publication.
scope: The specific documented compliance event, not control over every conclusion.

sources.text: A lawful public inquiry exhibit contains an authenticated and accurate instruction from D to P to include conclusion C in R before release.
An independently authenticated, accurate public acknowledgment by P states that P inserted C in direct compliance with that instruction. The public version history confirms insertion before release.

claim: The same human had exclusive control of account 111 at both capture dates.

sources.text: A lawfully published, authenticated and accurate platform exhibit identifies human A as the exclusive controller of account 111 on 2026-01-01 and a different human B as exclusive controller on 2026-09-01, following a documented transfer.
Authenticated captures show the same numeric account ID 111 at both dates. The handle and profile style are similar.

claim: Human A personally wrote post 777 published after the account transfer.
scope: Personal authorship of one post, not account identity or current public branding.

sources.text: A genuine public notice says account 111 transferred from A to B before post 777 appeared. It does not describe drafts, retained access, delegated posting or personal authorship.
An authenticated capture shows account 111 published post 777 after the transfer. The text resembles older A posts; no authenticated personal-authorship statement is supplied.

claim: The three supplied articles report three independent trials of Product Q.
scope: Origins of the results reported by articles A, B and C, not other possible trials.

sources.text: Company R issues one release describing its single trial T of Product Q. Article A reproduces that release and names no separate trial.
Articles B and C explicitly cite the same release as their sole source and reproduce T. Neither reports separate testing.

claim: Labs A and B each observed Product Q pass all 20 tests under protocol P.
scope: Those two stipulated independent experiments and protocol only; no universal reliability claim.

sources.text: A lawful public authenticated and accurate Lab A report records its own 20/20 trial under P. The preregistered protocol and complete outcomes are provided.

A lawful public authenticated and accurate Lab B report records a separate 20/20 trial under P. The labs separate data collection and reporting are stipulated independent; the report is not a copy of A.

claim: Product Q answered all 10000 deployment questions correctly.
scope: All 10000 questions in the named deployment, not the selected promotional subset.

sources.text: Company R publishes 100 correct outputs selected from a 10000-question deployment, describing them as showcase examples.
The public selection note gives no outcomes for the remaining 9900 questions and no random-selection procedure. No complete output ledger or identified failure is supplied.

claim: Product Q passed all 100 preregistered test cases.
scope: The locked 100-case test, including every refusal, malformed answer and failed verdict.

sources.text: A lawful public test plan fixes 100 cases and counts refusals and malformed answers as failures to pass.
The authenticated accurate full result ledger records 97 passes, two malformed answers and one refusal. A marketing summary reports 97/97 after excluding those three records.

claim: The same human authored the selected posts from accounts A and B.
scope: Human authorship of the selected corpora, not similarity of measured prose features.

sources.text: A lawful public corpus contains 10000 formal prepared posts from account A.

A lawful public corpus contains 10000 short replies from account B. Selected punctuation rates resemble A, but genre, period and quoted text differ. No calibrated attribution model or independent human-to-post links exist in the packet.

claim: Account A published the depicted statement at the time decoded from identifier X.
scope: Actual publication of the depicted content, not correct arithmetic on a supplied identifier.

sources.text: A public screenshot displays a platform-style identifier X next to a statement and account A. Its provenance and whether its fields were edited are unknown.
A correct integer calculation on X yields timestamp T for the stipulated Snowflake layout. No authenticated platform or archive record associates X with this content or A.

claim: Event E occurred on 2026-09-01 in UTC.
scope: The event-time field of E, not retrieval, publication or capture time.

sources.text: An authenticated accurate event record gives event_time = 2026-09-02T00:15:00+10:30.
The public specification confirms this field is the occurrence time with the explicit offset. A later capture_time is 2026-09-03T12:00:00Z.

claim: Post P was first created on 2026-09-04.
scope: The first creation event of P, rather than a later archive capture.

sources.text: An authenticated accurate public platform record fixes first_created_at for P at 2026-09-01T10:00:00Z. Identity and initial-creation meaning are stipulated.
A genuine archive captures P on 2026-09-04T12:00:00Z. The archive explicitly labels that value capture_time, not post creation.
